lead: A bearing holds a rotating shaft in place and lets it turn with as little resistance as possible. There are two families. Sliding contact bearings let one surface rub over another, separated by a film of oil. Rolling contact bearings put balls or rollers between the surfaces so they roll instead of rub. The choice fixes friction, starting torque, load capacity, speed limit, noise, space and cost. You meet both every day: the bush at the tail end of a pump shaft, and the sealed ball bearing inside a ceiling fan.
prereq: You need: Chapter 5.1 for viscosity and how a lubricant film carries load, and Unit 1, Foundations: Design Process and Stresses, for units and stress.

sections.h3: Sliding contact bearings and their materials

blocks.text: A sliding contact bearing, also called a plain bearing, carries load on two surfaces that slide over each other. A film of lubricant between them does the real work; when the film is complete, the metal never touches metal. A handful of shapes cover most applications.

items: Journal bearing: the shaft end (the journal) turns inside a sleeve, and the load is radial, at right angles to the axis. This is the commonest bearing in a pump or a turbine.
Bush: the replaceable sleeve itself. The same word is used for a one-piece plain bearing pressed into a housing.
Thrust bearing: takes load along the axis of the shaft.
Pivot: a small hemisphere or cone on the shaft end resting on a flat or conical seat, for light axial loads in instruments.
Collar: a ring fixed on the shaft that bears against a flat face of the housing, giving more rubbing area than a pivot.

blocks.text: Bearing materials are softer than the shaft, so they wear first and can embed grit instead of scoring the journal. Babbitt, a tin- or lead-base white metal, is soft and conforms well; it suits thin linings at high speed. Bronze is stronger and carries heavier loads at moderate speed. Cast iron is cheap, works at low speed and light load, and needs steady lubrication.

blocks.where: p is the bearing pressure in N/mm²; W is the radial load in N; L is the bearing length in mm; d is the journal diameter in mm. The product L d is the projected area.

blocks.text: A rolling contact bearing puts hardened steel balls or rollers between an inner ring and an outer ring. The rings sit on the shaft and in the housing, the rolling elements carry the load, and a cage keeps them evenly spaced. Because the contact rolls, friction and starting torque are far lower than in a plain bearing. Some syllabi call these antifriction bearings; the name means low friction, not zero friction.

items: Ball bearing: balls touch the rings at points, so it runs fast and takes radial load plus light axial load. This is the bearing inside a ceiling fan or a small motor.
Cylindrical roller bearing: rollers touch along a line, so radial capacity is higher, but it takes no axial load unless flanges are added.
Needle roller bearing: very thin, long rollers. It fits a small radial space, often without an inner ring, and suits oscillating joints such as a universal joint.
Tapered roller bearing: rollers and raceways are cones, so it takes radial and axial load together. Vehicle hubs and gearbox shafts use it.
Spherical roller bearing: two rows of barrel-shaped rollers in a spherical outer race. Heavy load, and it tolerates small misalignment between shaft and housing.

blocks.text: The friction torque in either bearing can be written with one coefficient, and the power lost follows from it. Use this only for an estimate; a real bearing catalogue gives its own friction figure.
T = μ W r    and    P = T ω
blocks.where: T is friction torque in N·m; μ is the coefficient of friction; W is the load in N; r is the shaft radius in m (r = d/2); P is friction power in W; ω is angular speed in rad/s, ω = 2πn/60 with n in rpm.

blocks.text: Choose a sliding bearing for heavy shock loads, very large shafts, quiet running or a split housing that must be assembled around the shaft. Choose a rolling bearing for low starting torque, small axial length, easy replacement and ready availability in standard sizes.
How well a sliding bearing performs depends on how much oil sits between the surfaces. Three regimes are named.

items: Boundary lubrication: the film is thinner than the surface roughness, so high spots touch. Friction is high, μ around 0.05 to 0.15. This is the state at starting, at very low speed and under very heavy load. Additives in the oil, not its viscosity, do the protecting here.
Mixed lubrication: part of the load is carried by a film and part by touching asperities. Most machines pass through this band while speeding up.

Hydrodynamic lubrication: a full film separates the surfaces and the pressure in the oil carries the whole load. Friction is low, μ around 0.001 to 0.01, and there is no wear. Chapter 5.3 shows how the rotating shaft builds that pressure.

blocks.text: Rolling bearings also run on a film, but a very thin one squeezed between curved surfaces; it is called an elastohydrodynamic film and it is why the right grease matters even though the metal looks dry.

examples.question: A shaft of diameter d = 100 mm carries a steady radial load W = 20 kN at n = 900 rpm. Compare the friction power lost in (a) a sliding contact bearing with μ = 0.02 and (b) a rolling contact bearing with μ = 0.002. Use T = μ W r and P = T ω.
steps: Data: d = 100 mm = 0.1 m, so radius r = d/2 = 0.05 m. W = 20 kN = 20 000 N. n = 900 rpm.
Convert speed to rad/s: ω = 2πn/60 = 2π × 900/60 = 94.2478 rad/s.
Sliding bearing torque: T = μ W r = 0.02 × 20 000 × 0.05 = 20 N·m.
Sliding bearing power: P = T ω = 20 × 94.2478 = 1884.96 W, about 1.885 kW.
Extra power lost by the sliding bearing = 1884.96 − 188.50 = 1696.46 W = 1.70 kW.
examples.answer: The rolling bearing loses 188.50 W against 1884.96 W for the sliding bearing, a saving of about 1.70 kW.

code.code:
import math

d = 0.100
r = d / 2
W = 20000.0
n = 900.0
w = 2 * math.pi * n / 60

for name, mu in (("sliding", 0.02), ("rolling", 0.002)):
    T = mu * W * r
    P = T * w
    print(name, "T =", round(T, 2), "N m", "P =", round(P, 2), "W")

traps: Using the shaft diameter instead of the radius 0.05 m in T = μ W r, which doubles the torque and the power.
Feeding rpm straight into P = T ω. Convert first: ω = 2πn/60, and only then multiply.
Reading 'antifriction bearing' as 'no friction'. A rolling bearing still has friction, and its starting torque is low but never zero.
Treating bush, babbitt and bronze as the same kind of thing: a bush is a shape, babbitt and bronze are lining materials.
Assuming a roller bearing is always the better choice. A cylindrical roller bearing carries no axial load and cannot match a ball bearing at high speed.

quiz.q: Name three materials used for sliding contact bearing linings and give one property of each.
quiz.a: Babbitt: soft, conforms well, embeds grit, good at high speed as a thin lining. Bronze: stronger, carries heavier loads at moderate speed. Cast iron: cheap, low speed and light load, needs steady lubrication.

quiz.q: Why is the bearing lining chosen softer than the shaft?
quiz.a: The lining wears first and can embed grit, so the expensive shaft and journal stay smooth. A soft lining also conforms to small misalignments, which spreads the load over a larger area.

quiz.q: Which rolling bearing type takes radial and axial load together, and which takes radial load only?
quiz.a: Tapered roller bearings and ball bearings take radial and axial load together. A plain cylindrical roller bearing takes radial load only.

quiz.q: Why does a spherical roller bearing allow the shaft and housing to be slightly misaligned?
quiz.a: Its outer raceway is a spherical surface, so the barrel-shaped rollers can tilt inside it and still carry load. Small angular errors from shaft deflection or housing distortion are absorbed instead of loading the edges.

quiz.q: A journal of diameter 60 mm and length 90 mm carries a radial load of 18 kN. Find the bearing pressure.
A rolling bearing with μ = 0.0015 carries W = 8 kN on a 50 mm shaft at n = 1440 rpm. Find the friction power.
A cold-storage conveyor must start under full load after hours idle. Explain which bearing family you would pick and why.
quiz.a: Pick a rolling bearing. After idle time the oil film in a sliding bearing has collapsed, so it starts in boundary lubrication with high friction and high starting torque. A rolling bearing starts on rolling contact with low torque, so the motor size and the belt slip risk both fall.

beyond: Not for the exam. In industry, bearing choice is driven by catalogue life and by the grease sealed inside: sealed-for-life ball bearings are why washing machines and fans need no lubrication schedule. Magnetic bearings and air bearings remove contact entirely for very high speed spindles and turbo-compressors. Condition monitoring reads vibration signatures to catch a spalled raceway before it fails.
